_comment: Coverage and listings, one entry per page. Every entry is backed by a screenshot in site/featured/ taken on the date in `captured`, whose SHA-256 is recorded here so a swapped image is detectable, and by a Wayback Machine copy where one could be made. tools/gen_site.py validates all of it and renders featured.html. `independent` is true when someone unconnected to the project wrote it; false means the project posted it itself. Dates are ISO 8601, UTC.

entries.title: Braino! Takes The Cheap Yellow Display To School
entries.said: A suite of applications flashed to a common Cheap Yellow Display to turn it into a legitimate educational tool; GPLv3, no ads, user accounts or cloud connectivity, and the parent picks which of the 40 games a child can reach.

entries.title: 2300円のボードが子ども用ゲーム機に、Makerが40本を公開
entries.title_en: A 2,300-yen board becomes a children's game console; a maker releases 40 games
entries.said: A Japanese maker-news report: 40 games in flash with no SD card, account or Wi-Fi needed, flashed over Web Serial, Bluetooth off by default, a PIN-protected administrator choosing what is shown, and a synthesised rather than recorded start-up voice.

entries.title: $9 CYD ESP32 Module Includes a 2.88-Inch LCD Screen
entries.said: Written from Hacktuber's video. Describes the firmware as an educational console with 31 built-in games, a periodic table, state maps and password-protected multi-user profiles, and names the author. It calls the firmware "Bro"; the count was 31 at the time.

entries.title: With This $9 CYD ESP32 Module You Can Do Anything...
entries.said: The first time somebody outside the project put Braino on real hardware on camera. The console is one segment of a tour of the board; the video had about 32,000 views when this page was made.

entries.title: Braino! Takes The Cheap Yellow Display To School
entries.said: The developer news feed picked the Hackaday piece up the same day, with its own summary: 40 selectable games, optional Bluetooth multiplayer, no ads, accounts or cloud connectivity.

entries.title: Listed under Applications in s0lness/awesome-esp32
entries.byline: Curated list; entries need linked proof of running on hardware
entries.said: Accepted into a hand-picked list of ESP32 projects, whose rules require proof the project ran on the named hardware and disclosure of self-nomination. The entry was proposed by the project and accepted by the list's maintainer.

entries.title: Listed in PROJECTS.md of witnessmenow/ESP32-Cheap-Yellow-Display
entries.byline: Brian Lough's community repository for the board
entries.said: The board's own community hub lists Braino among the projects that run on it. The entry was proposed by the project and merged by the hub's maintainers; it was updated from 31 to 40 games on 18 September 2026.

entries.title: Braino! — a 40-game learning console on a CYD
entries.said: The project's own write-up on Hackster: the bill of materials for every supported board, the story, and the two videos.

entries.title: Braino! — a 40-game learning console on a CYD
entries.byline: Posted by the project; entered in the Retro Computing contest
entries.said: The project page with six engineering logs: the 31-byte chess transport, Ludo's seed-derived dice, running with no heap allocation, the installer's version rollback, and the E32R40T reset loop.

entries.title: Braino! — ESP32 CYD Handheld Games Console
entries.said: The printable cases for the 2.8, 3.2 and 4-inch boards, with print profiles. Other people's prints and ratings appear on this page.

entries.title: Braino: a 40-game learning console on the cheap ESP32 touchscreen boards (open source)
entries.byline: Posted by the project in Projects > Showcase
entries.said: The engineering-first showcase post: no heap allocation, the 31-byte BLE advertisement, synthesised audio and the closed privacy list.
